summary.headline: Gallantt Ispat Q1 FY27: revenue ₹1,146 crore (+1.6% YoY), EBITDA ₹203 crore at 18% margin, PAT ₹124 crore at 11% margin, down YoY on coal and pellet shutdown.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was seasonally soft: TMT prices corrected through the monsoon quarter, and coal and freight costs rose amid Middle East tensions. Revenue was ₹1,146 crore versus ₹1,128 crore a year earlier and ₹1,205 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA of ₹203 crore (18% margin) and PAT margin of 11% were broadly flat sequentially but below Q1 FY26 (23% and 15%). Management says the 1.23 million tonne expansion and captive iron ore mines remain on schedule for H2 FY27 and FY28 respectively, and the company stays debt-free apart from working capital lines.

segments.name: TMT / long products
segments.commentary: TMT sales volume about 192,000 tonnes, flat YoY and down about 8% QoQ against a strong Q4. Management cites a sharp TMT price correction during the quarter, with the Gorakhpur rolling mill at about 66% utilisation versus 93% at the Gujarat unit.

segments.name: Billets
segments.commentary: Billet volumes rose 13% YoY and 38% QoQ, running ahead of the internal plan for the year.

segments.name: Pellets and sponge iron
segments.commentary: External sales fell both YoY and QoQ as more output was consumed captively for downstream TMT and billet production. The pellet plant was under planned annual maintenance, which the company says is now complete.

guidance_outlook: Capacity expansion from 1.0 million to 1.23 million tonnes (0.23 mt) to commission in H2 FY27; benefits to flow from H2.

Solar: 18 MW at Gujarat to commission in Q2 FY27 and 16-18 MW at Gaurav Pur (Gorakhpur) in Q4 FY27 (management cited 67 MW in one place and 16 MW in another, so the Gaurav Pur figure is unclear); the total solar programme is about 85 MW.
Captive iron ore mines (three: two in UP, one in Rajasthan) targeted for operation in FY28, with beneficiation plants. Exploration in UP expected to finish in 2-3 months.
Q2 expected to be muted on monsoon; management expects demand and pricing to pick up from Q3 (September-October onwards).
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 8-9% this year; management sees no demand-side problem in the medium term.
Medium-term growth plan to be shared next quarter. Management will evaluate debt or equity only where appropriate.
capex_capacity: Total KPEX programme about ₹3,000 crore: roughly half for mining and beneficiation, a solar build-out of about 85 MW, and capacity expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tonnes.
Q1 FY27 KPEX was ₹137 crore; about ₹800 crore spent over the last year. All funded by internal accruals.
Gujarat plant de-bottlenecking to complete within FY27 as planned.

Iron ore sourcing for the pellet plant: installed capacity about 8 lakh tonnes, raw feed need 9-9.5 lakh tonnes a year. Lloyd supplies about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a month, roughly 15-20% of the mix, mostly low-phosphorus.
demand_pricing: TMT prices fell well below where the quarter began, as Q1 seasonality combined with a sharp correction in long product realisation. Flat product prices held up better.
India turned a net steel importer in the quarter; the industry is seeking anti-dumping duties alongside existing safeguard duty.
The company claims a market share of over 25% in its addressable UP market. It uses two celebrity brand ambassadors (Ajay Devgn, and Janhvi Kapoor added recently).
Export is not a focus: Gorakhpur is inland and billet exports from Gujarat are occasional.

Coal sourcing: Gorakhpur power coal is 100% linkage (Coal India); DRI coal is 60-70% Indian and the rest South African imports. Gujarat power uses imported coal from Mundra and Kandla ports plus lignite blending.

qa_highlights.question: Iron ore and pellet sourcing, top suppliers and phosphorus handling?
qa_highlights.answer: Gorakhpur sources iron ore fines from Orissa-based suppliers, MP concentrate suppliers and Lloyd (Maharashtra). Lloyd's low-phosphorus ore is about 15-20% of the mix. High-phosphorus ore is handled by blending or ladle refining, depending on cost.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan beyond FY27 and how it will be funded; initiatives in UP and adjacent markets?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹3,000 crore KPEX, half for mining, plus solar and the capacity expansion, all funded from internal accruals. UP market share is above 25%, supported by brand campaigns, with expansion into other markets planned gradually.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a focus. Gorakhpur is inland and logistically unsuitable; Gujarat billet exports happen only occasionally.

qa_highlights.question: What drives margins and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites end-to-end integration from pellet or sponge iron to TMT, and no term loans. EBITDA/t was about ₹8,700 on a rolling basis, versus about ₹8,800 average in FY26. Solar and captive mines are expected to improve margins from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the import surge a flat-only issue or does it hit long products; demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat-product price falls spill over to long products. Management still expects 8-9% demand growth, with Q2 muted and Q3-Q4 better. Mining and solar timelines remain on track.

qa_highlights.question: Captive mines timeline and raw material cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: All three mines are targeted for FY28 operation. Raw material costs were up about 9% YoY, roughly half due to the pellet shutdown; iron ore and coal together added 4-5%. Coal is the main driver; logistics freight is the iron ore pressure.

risks_watch: Monsoon-driven Q2 weakness and whether TMT prices recover from Q3 as management expects.
Rising steel imports and the status of anti-dumping duty relief alongside existing safeguard duty.
Coal and freight cost trajectory amid Middle East tensions; the captive iron ore mines are not due until FY28, so raw material costs stay exposed in the interim.
Gorakhpur rolling mill utilisation at about 66% versus 93% at Gujarat; the company flagged this as a Q2 focus.
Cash balance fell QoQ alongside higher receivables and inventory; management expects normalisation as volumes and collections pick up.
Execution risk on mining approvals (environment and forest clearances) for the FY28 target, which management itself called aggressive.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term demand and the expansion timeline, but cautious on the near term: management openly flagged seasonal weakness, input cost pressure and pricing correction. Answers on mining timelines and margin direction were somewhat hedged, and the Q&A relied on repeated reassurance rather than new quantified guidance.
key_quotes: What we do take comfort from is that quarter on quarter our operating performance held its ground, which speaks to the resilience of our integrated model.
We remain on track on that front and there is no change to that timeline.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management expects demand and pricing to pick up from Q3 and says the 1.0 to 1.23 mt expansion commissions in H2 FY27, with mines in FY28, but no order or volume figures back the growth. Q1 revenue +1.6% YoY and EBITDA down about 20% YoY (₹203 cr vs ₹254 cr).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 23% YoY on TMT price correction and 9% raw material cost rise; management expects pricing to recover from Q3 and solar plus captive mines (FY28) to help margins, but no quantified margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 1.0 to 1.23 mt (0.23 mt, +23%) steel expansion is under construction and guided for H2 FY27 commissioning; 18 MW Gujarat solar in Q2 FY27 and 16-18 MW Gaurav Pur solar in Q4 FY27 (figure unclear).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 TMT volume flat YoY at ~192,000 t and Q2 expected muted on monsoon; billets up 13% YoY, and recovery from Q3 depends on demand and pricing, with Gorakhpur mill at 66% utilisation versus 93% at Gujarat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: About ₹3,000 crore KPEX programme already under way (₹137 cr in Q1, ~₹800 cr over last year), and a medium-term growth plan is to be shared next quarter, but no new capex figure was announced and utilisation is only 66% at Gorakhpur.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was raised; Q1 revenue was +1.6% YoY and EBITDA down about 20% YoY (₹203 cr vs ₹254 cr), with management flagging a weak Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a muted Q2 on monsoon, and the FY28 mine timeline was called aggressive, with approval risk (environment and forest clearances) not yet resolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or brand launch was discussed.

rows.label: Captive iron ore mines (three) with beneficiation for FY28
rows.why: Three mines (two UP, one Rajasthan) targeted for FY28 operation, with UP exploration finishing in 2-3 months; management called the timeline aggressive and mining approvals remain a risk.

rows.label: Net debt free as of 30 June 2026
rows.why: Borrowings limited to working capital lines with no term loans, and capex funded from internal accruals (₹800 cr over last year against ~₹3,000 cr programme).

rows.label: Receivables and inventory normalisation
rows.why: Cash fell QoQ on higher receivables and inventory; management expects normalisation as volumes and collections pick up from Q3.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 1.23 mt expansion timing, the 8-9% demand outlook and the debt-free balance sheet, but cautious on near-term monsoon weakness, input cost pressure and the TMT price correction; analysts pressed on margin sustainability and mine timelines, which got hedged answers.

oneOffs.what: No one-off gain in the year-ago base is stated in the brief; growth is weak because of TMT price correction and pellet shutdown, not a one-off

quality.why: Revenue grew only 1.6% YoY to ₹1,146 crore with TMT volume flat YoY (~192,000 t), so growth came from billets (+13% YoY) offset by a sharp TMT price correction; the brief names no one-off item in either quarter, so the weak growth reflects recurring price and volume dynamics rather than one-offs.
